title: Mapping the Loop Pair Strip onto a 3D Surface
full_prompt:
Create a 3D Manim visualization demonstrating how pairs of points on a 2D loop map to a 3D surface. The x and y coordinates of the surface represent the midpoint of the two points on the loop, while the z coordinate represents the distance between them. 

1. Define a 2D closed loop (e.g., an ellipse or a custom smooth SVG loop) on a flat plane.
2. Create two points, A and B, parameterized by u and v, which move along the loop. Show a line segment connecting them.
3. Construct a 3D coordinate system. Define a parametric surface where each point (u, v) maps to (midpoint_x, midpoint_y, distance_AB).
4. Render this parametric surface in 3D, showing how the boundary of the surface corresponds to u = v (where distance is 0, lying flat on the loop itself).
5. Synchronize the movement of points A and B on the 2D loop with a glowing tracker dot on the 3D surface that represents their current midpoint and distance.
6. Use a 3D camera rotation to showcase the topological structure of the surface, highlighting how it forms a strip (or Möbius strip representation) bounded by the loop itself.

common_failure_modes.pattern: Camera orientation conflicts between 2D loop display and 3D surface display
common_failure_modes.note: Ensure the 2D loop is correctly projected or positioned in the 3D scene so it does not clip or disappear when the camera rotates.

common_failure_modes.pattern: Parametric surface rendering performance issues due to high sample density
common_failure_modes.note: Keep u and v resolution reasonable (e.g., 50x50) to avoid slow rendering times in Manim.

common_failure_modes.pattern: Discontinuity at the boundary of the loop parameterization
common_failure_modes.note: Ensure smooth interpolation of the loop points when u or v wraps around from 1.0 to 0.0.
